verses.zh: 义人死亡，无人放在心上；虔诚人被收去，无人思念。这义人被收去是免了将来的祸患；
verses.en: The godly[NOTE:1] perish,but no one cares.[NOTE:2] Honest people disappear,[NOTE:3] when no one[NOTE:4] minds[NOTE:5] that the godly[NOTE:6] disappear[NOTE:7] because of[NOTE:8] evil.[NOTE:9]
notes: Or “righteous” (KJV, NASB, NIV, NRSV, NLT); NAB “the just man”; TEV “Good people.”
Or perhaps, “understands.” Heb “and there is no man who sets [it] upon [his] heart.”
Heb “Men of loyalty are taken away.” The Niphal of אָסַף (ʾasaf) here means “to die.”
The Hebrew term בְּאֵין (beʾen) often has the nuance “when there is no.” See Prov 8:24; 11; 14; 14:4; 15:22; 26:20; 29:18.
Or “realizes”; Heb “understands” (so NASB, NIV, NRSV).
Or “righteous” (KJV, NASB, NIV, NRSV, NLT); NAB “the just man.”
Heb “are taken away.” The Niphal of אָסַף (ʾasaf) here means “to die.”

The term מִפְּנֵי (mippene, “from the face of”) often has a causal nuance. It also appears with the Niphal of אָסַף (ʾasaph, “gather”) in 2 Chr 12:5: אֲשֶׁר־נֶאֶסְפוּ אֶל־יְרוּשָׁלַםִ מִפְּנֵי שִׁישָׁק (ʾasher-neʾespu ʾel-yerushalaim mippene shishaq, “who had gathered at Jerusalem because of [i.e., due to fear of] Shishak”).

The translation assumes that this verse, in proverbial fashion, laments society’s apathy over the persecution of the godly. The second half of the verse observes that such apathy results in more widespread oppression. Since the next verse pictures the godly being taken to a place of rest, some interpret the second half of v. 1 in a more positive vein. According to proponents of this view, God removes the godly so that they might be spared suffering and calamity, a fact which the general populace fails to realize.

verses.zh: 他们得享（原文是进入）平安。素行正直的，各人在坟里（原文是床上）安歇。
verses.en: Those who live uprightly enter a place of peace;they rest on their beds.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “he enters peace, they rest on their beds, the one who walks straight ahead of himself.” The tomb is here viewed in a fairly positive way as a place where the dead are at peace and sleep undisturbed.

verses.zh: 你们这些巫婆的儿子，奸夫和妓女的种子，都要前来！
verses.en: “But approach, you sons of omen readers,you offspring of adulteresses and prostitutes![NOTE:1]
notes: The Hebrew text reads literally, “offspring of an adulterer [masculine] and [one who] has committed adultery.” Perhaps the text has suffered from transposition of vav (ו) and tav (ת) and מְנָאֵף וַתִּזְנֶה (menaʾef vattizneh) should be emended to מְנָאֶפֶת וְזֹנָה (menaʾefet vezonah, “an adulteress and a prostitute”). Both singular nouns would be understood in a collective sense. Most modern English versions render both forms as nouns.

verses.zh: 你们向谁戏笑？向谁张口吐舌呢？你们岂不是悖逆的儿女，虚谎的种类呢？
verses.en: At whom are you laughing?At whom are you opening your mouthand sticking out your tongue?You are the children of rebels,the offspring of liars,[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “Are you not children of rebellion, offspring of a lie?” The rhetorical question anticipates the answer, “Of course you are!”

verses.zh: 你们在橡树中间，在各青翠树下欲火攻心；在山谷间，在石穴下杀了儿女；
verses.en: you who inflame your lusts[NOTE:1] among the oaks[NOTE:2] and under every green tree,who slaughter children near the streams under the rocky overhangs.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “inflame yourselves”; NRSV “burn with lust.” This verse alludes to the practice of ritual sex that accompanied pagan fertility rites.

The term אֵלִים (ʾelim) may be from a root meaning “mighty ones,” referring to mighty trees. The form may also refer to “gods,” a less common masculine plural of (ʾel). This would fit the context of idolatry (lusting after gods).
This apparently alludes to the practice of child sacrifice (cf. TEV, CEV, NLT).

verses.zh: 在谷中光滑石头里有你的分。这些就是你所得的分；你也向他浇了奠祭，献了供物，因这事我岂能容忍吗？
verses.en: Among the smooth stones of the stream are the idols you love;they, they are the object of your devotion.[NOTE:1] You pour out liquid offerings to them,you make an offering.Because of these things how can I relent from judgment?[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “among the smooth stones of the stream [is] your portion, they, they [are] your lot.” The next line indicates idols are in view.

The text reads literally as a question, “Because of these am I relenting?” However, the initial letter he may be dittographic (note the final he [ה] on the preceding word). In this case one could understand the verb in the sense of “Because of these I will seek vengeance,” as in 1:24. If the prefixed interrogative particle is retained at the beginning of the sentence, then the question is rhetorical, with the Niphal of נָחָם (nakham) probably being used in the sense of “relent, change one’s mind.”

verses.zh: 你在高而又高的山上安设床榻，也上那里去献祭。
verses.en: On every high, elevated hill you prepare your bed;you go up there to offer sacrifices.

verses.zh: 你在门后，在门框后，立起你的纪念；向外人赤露，又上去扩张床榻，与他们立约；你在那里看见他们的床就甚喜爱。
verses.en: Behind the door and doorpost you put your symbols.[NOTE:1] Indeed,[NOTE:2] you depart from me[NOTE:3] and go upand invite them into bed with you.[NOTE:4] You purchase favors from them;[NOTE:5] you love their bed,and gaze longingly[NOTE:6] on their naked bodies.[NOTE:7]
notes: The precise referent of זִכָּרוֹן (zikkaron) in this context is uncertain. Elsewhere the word refers to a memorial or commemorative sign. Here it likely refers to some type of idolatrous symbol.
Or “for” (KJV, NRSV).

The Hebrew text reads literally, “from me you uncover.” The translation assumes an emendation of the Piel form גִּלִּית (gillit, “you uncover”), which has no object expressed here, to the Qal גָּלִית (galit, “you depart”).
Heb “you make wide your bed” (NASB similar).

Heb “and you [second masculine singular, unless the form be taken as third feminine singular] cut for yourself [feminine singular] from them.” Most English translations retain the MT reading in spite of at least three problems. This section makes significant use of feminine verbs and noun suffixes because of the sexual imagery. The verb in question is likely a second person masculine singular verb. Nevertheless, this kind of fluctuation in gender appears elsewhere (GKC 127-28 §47.k and 462 §144.p; cf. Jer 3:5; Ezek 22:4; 23:32; cf. J. N. Oswalt, Isaiah [NICOT], 2:473, n. 13). Secondly, when this verbal root signifies establishing a covenant, it is normally accompanied by the noun for “covenant” (בְּרִית, berit). Finally, this juxtaposition of the verb “to cut” and “covenant” normally is followed by the preposition “with,” while here it is “from.” The translation above assumes an emendation of וַתִּכְרָת (vatikhrat, “and you cut”) to וְכָרִית (vekharit, “and you purchase”) from the root כָּרָה (kharah); see HALOT 497 s.v. II כרה.
The Hebrew text has simply חָזָה (khazah, “gaze”). The adverb “longingly” is interpretive (see the context, where sexual lust is depicted).
Heb “[at] a hand you gaze.” The term יָד (yad, “hand”) probably has the sense of “power, manhood” here, where it is used, as in Ugaritic, as a euphemism for the genitals. See HALOT 387 s.v. I יָד.

verses.zh: 你把油带到王那里，又多加香料，打发使者往远方去，自卑自贱直到阴间，
verses.en: You take olive oil as tribute[NOTE:1] to your king,[NOTE:2] along with many perfumes.[NOTE:3] You send your messengers to a distant place;you go all the way to Sheol.[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “you journey with oil.”

Heb “the king.” Since the context refers to idolatry and child sacrifice (see v. 5), some emend מֶלֶך (melekh, “king”) to “Molech.” Perhaps Israel’s devotion to her idols is likened here to a subject taking tribute to a ruler.
Heb “and you multiply your perfumes.”
Israel’s devotion to her idols is inordinate, irrational, and self-destructive.

verses.zh: 你因路远疲倦，却不说这是枉然；你以为有复兴之力，所以不觉疲惫。
verses.en: Because of the long distance you must travel, you get tired,[NOTE:1] but you do not say, ‘I give up.’[NOTE:2] You get renewed energy,[NOTE:3] so you don’t collapse.[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “by the greatness [i.e., “length,” see BDB 914 s.v. רֹב 2] of your way you get tired.”
Heb “it is hopeless” (so NAB, NASB, NIV); NRSV “It is useless.”
Heb “the life of your hand you find.” The term חַיָּה (khayyah, “life”) is here used in the sense of “renewal” (see BDB 312 s.v.) while יָד (yad) is used of “strength.”
Heb “you do not grow weak.”

verses.zh: 你怕谁？因谁恐惧？竟说谎，不记念我，又不将这事放在心上。我不是许久闭口不言，你仍不怕我吗？
verses.en: Whom are you worried about?Whom do you fear, that you would act so deceitfullyand not remember meor think about me?[NOTE:1] Because I have been silent for so long,[NOTE:2] you are not afraid of me.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “you do not place [it] on your heart.”
Heb “Is it not [because] I have been silent, and from long ago?”
God’s patience with sinful Israel has caused them to think that they can sin with impunity and suffer no consequences.

verses.zh: 我要指明你的公义；至于你所行的都必与你无益。
verses.en: I will denounce your so-called righteousness and your deeds,[NOTE:1] but they will not help you.
notes: Heb “I, I will declare your righteousness and your deeds.”

verses.zh: 你哀求的时候，让你所聚集的拯救你吧！风要把他们刮散，一口气要把他们都吹去。但那投靠我的必得地土，必承受我的圣山为业。
verses.en: When you cry out for help, let your idols[NOTE:1] help you!The wind blows them all away,[NOTE:2] a breeze carries them away.[NOTE:3] But the one who looks to me for help[NOTE:4] will inherit the landand will have access to[NOTE:5] my holy mountain.”
notes: The Hebrew text has קִבּוּצַיִךְ (qibbutsayikh, “your gatherings”), an otherwise unattested noun from the verbal root קָבַץ (qavats, “gather”). Perhaps this alludes to their religious assemblies and by metonymy to their rituals. Since idolatry is a prominent theme in the context, some understand this as a reference to a collection of idols. The second half of the verse also favors this view.
Heb “all of them a wind lifts up.”
Heb “a breath takes [them] away.”
Or “seeks refuge in me.” “Seeking refuge” is a metonymy for “being loyal to.”
Heb “possess, own.” The point seems to be that he will have free access to God’s presence, as if God’s temple mount were his personal possession.

verses.zh: 耶和华要说：你们修筑修筑，预备道路，将绊脚石从我百姓的路中除掉。
verses.en: He says,[NOTE:1] “Build it! Build it! Clear a way!Remove all the obstacles out of the way of my people!”
notes: Since God is speaking throughout this context, perhaps we should emend the text to “and I say.” However, divine speech is introduced in v. 15.

verses.zh: 因为那至高至上、永远长存（原文是住在永远）名为圣者的如此说：我住在至高至圣的所在，也与心灵痛悔谦卑的人同居；要使谦卑人的灵苏醒，也使痛悔人的心苏醒。
verses.en: For this is what the high and exalted one says,the one who rules[NOTE:1] forever, whose name is holy:“I dwell in an exalted and holy place,but also with the discouraged and humiliated,[NOTE:2] in order to cheer up the humiliatedand to encourage the discouraged.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “the one who dwells forever.” שֹׁכֵן עַד (shokhen ʿad) is sometimes translated “the one who lives forever,” and understood as a reference to God’s eternal existence. However, the immediately preceding and following descriptions (“high and exalted” and “holy”) emphasize his sovereign rule. In the next line, he declares, “I dwell in an exalted and holy [place],” which refers to the place from which he rules. Therefore it is more likely that שֹׁכֵן עַד (shokhen ʿad) means “I dwell [in my lofty palace] forever” and refers to God’s eternal kingship.

Heb “and also with the crushed and lowly of spirit.” This may refer to the repentant who have humbled themselves (see 66:2) or more generally to the exiles who have experienced discouragement and humiliation.
Heb “to restore the lowly of spirit and to restore the heart of the crushed.”

verses.zh: 我必不永远相争，也不长久发怒，恐怕我所造的人与灵性都必发昏。
verses.en: For I will not be hostile[NOTE:1] foreveror perpetually angry,for then man’s spirit would grow faint before me,[NOTE:2] the life-giving breath I created.
notes: Or perhaps, “argue,” or “accuse” (so NAB, NIV, NRSV).
Heb “for a spirit from before me would be faint.”

verses.zh: 因他贪婪的罪孽，我就发怒击打他；我向他掩面发怒，他却仍然随心背道。
verses.en: I was angry because of their sinful greed;I attacked them and angrily rejected them,[NOTE:1] yet they remained disobedient and stubborn.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “and I struck him, hiding, and I was angry.” פָּנִים (panim, “face”) is the implied object of “hiding.”
Heb “and he walked [as an] apostate in the way of his heart.”

verses.zh: 我看见他所行的道，也要医治他；又要引导他，使他和那一同伤心的人再得安慰。
verses.en: I have seen their behavior,[NOTE:1] but I will heal them. I will lead[NOTE:2] them,and I will provide comfort[NOTE:3] to them and those who mourn with them.[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “his ways” (so KJV, NASB, NIV84); NIV11 “their ways”; TEV “how they acted.”

The MT has וְאַנְחֵהוּ (veʾankhehu) from נָחָה (nakhah) “I will lead them,” but the consonantal text may also be read as וַאֲנִחֵהוּ (vaʾanikhehu) from נוּחַ (nuakh) “I will give them rest.” The MT is supported by Aquila and the Vulgate, though 1QIsaa omits the verb and the LXX and Targum offer mixed evidence.

The verb וַאֲשַׁלֵּם (vaʾashallem), the Piel form of the verb שָׁלֵם (shalem), means “to make whole, make restitution, compensate, reward” (HALOT 1534, s.v.). The noun נִחֻמִים (nikhumim) uses the plural form for the abstract concept, “comfort.” The Lord will bestow comfort as restitution to Israel.

Heb “to him and to his mourners.” Since Israel is represented by the singular pronoun “to him” (rendered as plural “them” for style throughout vv. 17-19), those who mourn for, or with, him are likely religious converts or others who sympathize with Israel (see J. D. W. Watts, Isaiah [WBC], 25:835).

verses.zh: 我造就嘴唇的果子；愿平安康泰归与远处的人，也归与近处的人；并且我要医治他。这是耶和华说的。
verses.en: I am the one who gives them reason to celebrate.[NOTE:1] Complete prosperity[NOTE:2] is available both to those who are far away and those who are nearby,”says the Lord, “and I will heal them.
notes: The Hebrew text has literally, “one who creates fruit of lips.” Perhaps the pronoun אֲנִי (ʾani) should be inserted after the participle; it may have been accidentally omitted by haplography: נוּב שְׂפָתָיִם [אֲנִי] בּוֹרֵי (boreʾ [ʾani] nuv sefatayim). “Fruit of the lips” is often understood as a metonymy for praise; perhaps it refers more generally to joyful shouts (see v. 18).
Heb “Peace, peace.” The repetition of the noun emphasizes degree.

verses.zh: 惟独恶人，好像翻腾的海，不得平静；其中的水常涌出污秽和淤泥来。
verses.en: But the wicked are like a surging seathat is unable to be quiet;its waves toss up mud and sand.

verses.zh: 我的　神说：恶人必不得平安！
verses.en: There will be no prosperity,” says my God, “for the wicked.”

READING CYCLE THREE (see
"Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which
means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the
light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not
relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare
your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is
the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every
paragraph has one and only one subject.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

- Obviously the context of Israel's sin continues from Isaiah 56.

- This describes the OT theological concept of "the two ways"; one of life and peace and the other of self,
sin, and ruin (cf. Deut. 30:15,19; Psalm 1).

- H. C. Leupold makes the interesting comment (p. 271) that as Isaiah 56 ended on faithless leaders,
Isaiah 57 deals with faithless people.

- The setting of the idolatry is not Mesopotamia but Canaan's fertility cults (i.e. Ba'al,
Asherah, Molech). This reached its apex under King Manasseh.

SPECIAL TOPIC: MOLECH

SPECIAL TOPIC: FERTILITY WORSHIP OF THE ANE

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: ISAIAH 57:1-10

1"The righteous man perishes, and no man takes it to heart;

And devout men are taken away, while no one understands.

For the righteous man is taken away from evil,

2He enters into peace;

They rest in their beds,

Each one who walked in his upright way.

3But come here, you sons of a sorceress,

Offspring of an adulterer and a prostitute.

4Against whom do you jest?

Against whom do you open wide your mouth

And stick out your tongue?

Are you not children of rebellion,

Offspring of deceit,

5Who inflame yourselves among the oaks,

Under every luxuriant tree,

Who slaughter the children in the ravines,

Under the clefts of the crags?

6Among the smooth stones of the ravine

Is your portion, they are your lot;

Even to them you have poured out a drink offering,

You have made a grain offering.

Shall I relent concerning these things?

7Upon a high and lofty mountain

You have made your bed.

You also went up there to offer sacrifice.

8Behind the door and the doorpost

You have set up your sign;

Indeed, far removed from Me, you have uncovered yourself,

And have gone up and made your bed wide.

And you have made an agreement for yourself with them,

You have loved their bed,

You have looked on their manhood.

9You have journeyed to the king with oil

And increased your perfumes;

You have sent your envoys a great distance

And made them go down to Sheol.

10You were tired out by the length of your road,

Yet you did not say, 'It is hopeless.'

You found renewed strength,

Therefore you did not faint."

57:1 Evil triumphs when the righteous are persecuted and murdered, and no one seems to care!

- no man takes it to heart

- no one understands

SPECIAL TOPIC: RIGHTEOUSNESS

▣ "is taken away from evil" As the wicked seek self and sin, the righteous are delivered
from the terrible influence of the Fall (cf. Genesis 3; 6:5,11-12).

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE FALL OF MANKIND

▣ The last line of v. 1 (NASB) seems in conflict with the meaning of the first two lines.

- The JPSOA adjusts this by translating, "That because of evil the righteous are taken away."

- The TEV has "But when they die, no calamity can hurt them."

- The NJB has "Yes, because of the evil times the upright is taken off."

- The REB has "The righteous are swept away by the onset of evil."

However, v. 2 implies that it is YHWH who takes them away to a place of blessing. Death for
faithful followers is a reunion, not a separation (i.e. 2 Cor. 5:6,8; Heb. 11:13-16).

57:2 This verse describes the spiritual condition of the righteous man.

- enters into peace (because of Isa. 57:1 this must be mental; see SPECIAL TOPIC: PEACE [OT])

- rest in their beds (BDB 1012). There is a word play on this word used here of the righteous,
but in Isa. 57:7,8, of the wicked (i.e. "they rest in their beds").

- bed for sleep (JPSOA, NRSV, NJB)

- bed for sex (cf. vv. 7,8)

- the grave (NET, REB, TEV, LXX)

- walked in his upright way (i.e. lifestyle faithfulness; see SPECIAL TOPIC: THE PATH, THE WAY)

57:3-4 These verses describe the wicked ones mentioned in Isa. 57:1. They are characterized as

- sons of a sorcerer (BDB 778 II, cf. Isa. 2:6; Jer. 27:9; Micah 5:12; see SPECIAL TOPIC: MAGIC, #10)

- offspring of an adulterer (BDB 610)

- offspring of a prostitute (BDB 275)

YHWH calls them to approach (Qal IMPERATIVE, BDB 897, KB 1132) His presence for judgment.

- offspring of deceit (BDB 833)

- against whom do you jest

- against whom do you open wide your mouth

- against whom do you stick out your tongue (these described their accusations against the righteous)

- children of rebellion (BDB 1055)

57:5-6 The idolatry is described as

- inflame yourself among the oaks (Niphal PARTICIPLE, BDB 328, KB 328). This
refers to the fertility worship of Ba'al and Asherah, i.e. Deut. 12:2; 1 Kgs. 14:23; 2 Kgs. 17:10; Jer. 2:20; 23-28; 31:6-13; Ezek. 6:13; 20:28; Hosea 4:13)

- slaughter the children (Qal PARTICIPLE, BDB 1006, KB 1458, this
refers to the worship of Molech; see SPECIAL TOPIC: MOLECH)

- pour out a libation (Qal PERFECT, BB 1049, KB 1629)

- make a grain offering (Hiphil PERFECT, BDB 748, KB 828)

SPECIAL TOPIC: FERTILITY WORSHIP OF THE ANCIENT NEAR EAST

57:6a The reference to which this line relates is uncertain.

- the cultic trees of Asherah worship, v. 5a,b

- the place of sacrificing children (i.e. valley of Hinnom), v. 5c

- associated with the "clefts of the crags," v. 5d

- another place of fertility worship (i.e. sacrifice), v. 7c

- drink offerings, v. 6c

- grain offerings, v. 6d

- the promiscuity of v. 7a,b

- Rotherham's Emphasized Bible, p. 701, suggests the meaning is "in open places in the valley," these
fertility worshipers expose themselves (i.e. no modesty or sense of morality).

57:6e

NASB
"Shall I relent concerning these things"

NKJV
"Should I receive comfort in these"

NRSV
"Shall I be appeased for these things"

TEV
"Do you think I am pleased with all this"

LXX
"Shall I not therefore be angry for these things"

Peshitta
"Should I receive comfort in these things"

JPSOA
"Should I relent in the face of these"

REB
"In spite of this am I to relent"

The Israelites' fertility worship, even if done in YHWH's name (i.e. the golden calves at Dan and Bethel), was unacceptable! God
had no choice but to judge His people in order to restore proper worship. This is possibly a rhetorical question (see NET Bible, p. 1274, #13)

57:7 This refers to the Ba'al and Asherah altars which were placed on the tops of
hills (cf. Deut. 12:2; 2 Kgs. 17:10; Jer. 3:6; 17:2; Hosea 4:13). The phrase "made their bed" refers to the ritual
sexual activities offerred for the fertility of the land, herds, and human population (cf. Isa. 57:8b-d).

SPECIAL TOPIC: HUMAN SEXUALITY

57:8 The first two lines are ambiguous. This could refer to an idolatrous image set up

The MT has "cut" (BDB 503, #4; KB 500, Qal IMPERFECT with waw),
which often refers to "cutting a covenant" (cf. Gen. 26:28; 31:44; 1 Sam. 11:1; Ps. 83:5; Isa. 55:3; 61:8; Hosea 12:1),
but here, it does not seem to fit. The NET Bible assumes an emendation.

- ותכות ‒ MT, "to cut"

Context, context, context must determine meaning.

57:8g

NASB
"you have looked on their manhood"

NKJV
"where you saw their hand"

TEV
"there you satisfy your lust"

NJB
"with your eyes on the sacred symbol"

JPSOA
"you have chosen lust"

NRSV, NIV, Peshitta
"where you saw their nakedness"

NET Bible
"gaze longingly on their genitals"

The problem is the word יד (BDB 388, KB 386), which is literally "hand."

- In Ugaritic ידד means "love" or "genitals."

- In Arabic ידו means "penis" (cf. NIDOTTE, vol 2, p. 56).

- It could refer to "sexual strength" here in a fertility worship sense.

There are several euphemisms used by Hebrew authors to refer to the sex organs (another example is "feet,"
BDB 919, cf. Exod. 4:25; Deut. 28:57; Jdg. 3:24; Ruth 3:8; 1 Sam. 24:3; Ezek. 16:25).

57:9-10 This seems to refer to the political gifts to assure their safety against foreign invasion.

whose name has the same consonants as "king" (mlk) in Hebrew. The UBS Text Project, p. 150, gives "king" a B rating (some doubt).

This term (BDB 851 II) usually refers to ambassador type messengers (cf. Isa. 18:2;

Molech was the god of the netherworld.

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: ISAIAH 57:11-13

11"Of whom were you worried and fearful

When you lied, and did not remember Me

Nor give Me a thought?

Was I not silent even for a long time

So you do not fear Me?

12I will declare your righteousness and your deeds,

But they will not profit you.

13When you cry out, let your collection of idols deliver you.

But the wind will carry all of them up,

And a breath will take them away.

But he who takes refuge in Me will inherit the land

And will possess My holy mountain."

57:11-13 This strophe starts with a series of questions from YHWH to His faithless covenant
people. The tragedy was that they were "religious" (cf. Isa. 57:12,13a) but had

- not remembered (Qal PERFECT, BDB 269, KB 269, negated) Him

- nor give Me a thought (lit. "lay it to heart of you," Qal PERFECT, BDB 962, KB 1321, negated)

The reasons they had neglected YHWH was His silence (Isa. 57:11d). This may refer to true
prophets who were not sent or at least not heard.

The idols are "vanity" and "emptiness." The wind will carry them away and along with
them, those who trust in them.

JPSOA

The JPSOA mentions an emendation that results in "and shut my eyes" (p. 898),
which is followed by REB and NAB. The same Hebrew consonants ומעלם
can be translated "and from eternity" or "and being hidden" (UBS Text Project, p. 151; it refers to "and from eternity").

The immediate context does not make sense using "eternity." For a period of time (i.e. 70 years),
YHWH refused to help His covenant people because of their covenant disobedience and idolatry. He hid His face
from them and did not respond to their prayers. It may have seemed to them to be an eternity!

57:14 There is a series of IMPERATIVES whereby YHWH commands that all necessary
preparations be made for His faithful ones to return from exile (cf. Isa. 40:3-4; 62:10).

- build up (twice) ‒ Qal IMPERATIVE, BDB 699, KB 757

- prepare the way ‒ Piel IMPERATIVE, BDB 815, KB 937

- remove every obstacle ‒ Hiphil IMPERATIVE, BDB 926, KB 1202

57:15 Notice the titles and characterizations of God.

- the high One ‒ Qal PARTICIPLE, BDB 926, KB 1202 (same VERB
used in Isa. 57:14 translated "remove," i.e. lift up)

- the exalted One ‒ Niphal PARTICIPLE, BDB 669, KB 724 (same VERB
used in Isa. 57:7,13, but in different senses)

- who lives forever ‒ Qal PARTICIPLE, BDB 1014, KB 1496, (lit. "who inhabits
eternity"). The NET Bible [p. 1275] thinks in this context it should be understood as "the One who rules forever." This may
be true because of Exod. 15:18; Ps. 10:16.

- whose name is Holy (see
SPECIAL TOPIC: HOLY)

- dwells on a high and holy place ‒ Qal IMPERFECT, BDB 1014, KB 1496
(in contrast to the fertility gods)

- with a contrite (BDB 194 I) and lowly (BDB 1050) spirit (BDB 924)

- to revive the heart of the contrite ‒ Hiphil INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT, BDB 310, KB 309, used twice

- of YHWH, #6

- of His faithful

Notice in the great covenant God wants to dwell with believing, faithful followers (v. 15d).

57:16a-b This continues a description of YHWH by YHWH.

- "I will not contend forever" ‒ Qal IMPERFECT, BDB 936, KB 1224, cf. Gen. 6:3

- "neither will I always be angry" ‒ Qal IMPERFECT, BDB 893, KB 1124, cf.
Ps. 79:5; 85:5; 103:9; Micah 7:18-19

This should not be interpreted as a period of time set by God after which His grace ceases, but
the reality that when humans ignore and violate His word and will, there is a terrible consequence of hardening.
The human heart becomes unable to hear and respond!

It is interesting that the OT contrasts the human emotions of love and anger when describing God.

- love is long lasting and sure ‒ Deut. 5:10; 7:9; Ps. 30:5; Isa. 54:7-8; Jer. 31:3

- anger is short lived ‒ Deut. 5:9; Ps. 30:5; Isa. 26:20; 54:7-8; 57:16-19

57:16c-d YHWH reveals the reasons why He does not remain angry (see
SPECIAL TOPIC: GOD DESCRIBED AS HUMAN [anthropomorphism]). This is very similar to Ps. 103:8-14.

- for the spirit (see SPECIAL TOPIC: SPIRIT IN THE BIBLE) would grow faint before Me

- the breath would grow faint

Notice the parallelism of "spirit" (BDB 924) and "breath" (BDB 675) as in Isa. 42:5. The frail
physical and now psychological condition of fallen mankind cannot endure the silence (Isa. 57:11,17) and
anger (Isa. 57:16,17) of their Creator and Redeemer!

57:19a "creating the praise of the lips" Literally, "the fruit of the lips." This, and similar phrases like it (i.e. Lev. 7:12),
became the Jewish community's way to speak of sacrifice when there was no temple or temple access. Modern Judaism cannot
do Mosaic practice because there is no place to offer sacrifice or approach Him on feast days.

The Jewish believer, whoever it was, of the book of Hebrews uses this same sacrificial terminology in Heb. 13:15
to denote Christian worship.

57:19b In context, this refers to the faithful remnant who are in Palestine and those still in exile.

In the NT, this text relates to

- Jewish pilgrims to Jerusalen at Passover and residents of Jerusalem ‒ Acts 2:37-42

- all believng human beings ‒ Eph. 2:11-3:13 (esp. Eph. 2:17)

This transfer of promises to the faithful OT remnant is expanded in the NT to all human beings.
